questions.q: Complete the saying of the Prophet quoted at the start of the article: “I have been sent to…”
options: “…perfect the code of high ethics.”
This is the saying with which the article opens.
“…build great cities.”
This is not part of the saying.
“…gather wealth for the poor.”
This is not the saying quoted here.
“…rule over the nations.”
The Prophet’s mission is described in terms of character, not rule.
questions.rationale: Worship alone does not make a perfect believer; one must also keep the highest standard of moral character in dealing with others.

questions.q: How does the article describe true religiosity?
options: Visiting holy persons for their prayers
The article calls relying on this a fallacy.
Counting words on a rosary
This is one of the examples of mere ritual.
A conscious act, rather than the observance of a set of rituals
Religion has to be discovered at a conscious level.
Following the customs of one’s family
The article asks for awareness, not inherited custom.
questions.rationale: People use reason in worldly matters but not in religion. A person should make his religious life a life of awareness, just like his worldly life.

questions.q: Of what is old age a potent reminder, according to the article?
options: The pleasures of youth
The article looks forward, not back.
The Hereafter
Old age signals the approach of death and prompts introspection.
The need to gather more wealth
Nothing of the kind is suggested.
The weakness of others
The lesson is for oneself.
questions.rationale: The Quran asks: ‘Did We not make your life long enough to take warning?’ (35: 37). The weakening of the body awakens the mind to what lies ahead.

options: Travellers
This is not the meaning given.
Judges
They came to the Prophet for judgement; the word does not mean judges.
Scholars
This is not the meaning given.
Supporters or helpers
They were the people of Madinah who supported the early Muslims.
questions.rationale: Two of the Ansar brought a long-standing inheritance dispute to the Prophet. The Quran commands: ‘When you judge between people, judge with justice.’ (4: 58)

questions.q: How did Ernest Psichari describe silence?
options: “A bit of heaven that comes down to earth”
He also called silence the language of nature.
“The absence of all thought”
The article presents silence as expanding our consciousness.
“A sign of weakness”
The article praises silence.
“The enemy of friendship”
This is not in the article.
questions.rationale: When one embraces silence, a sense of harmony with nature emerges, and one connects with the self and with the divine.

questions.q: Which saying of Anne Bronte does the article quote?
options: “All that glitters is not gold.”
This is not the saying quoted.
“Where there is a will, there is a way.”
This is not the saying quoted.
“There is always a ‘but’ in this imperfect world.”
The article calls this a wise saying.
“The pen is mightier than the sword.”
This is not the saying quoted.
questions.rationale: This world is made for trial, so the ideal state is not achievable here. One must acknowledge the barricades of ‘buts’ and plan realistically.

questions.q: What do the limitations of justice in this world point to, according to the article?
options: The need to abolish all laws
The article says law is needed for the smooth running of society.
The coming of another, unlimited world where full justice will be done
There, punishment will be proportionate to the crime.
That justice is only an idea
The article affirms that justice will be done in the next world.
That crime should go unpunished
The article says the opposite.
questions.rationale: Worldly punishment can never be proportionate to a crime such as the murder of two children. This shortfall necessitates a world that makes up for it.

questions.q: What name does the article give to the “disease” of wealth in America?
options: “Gold fever”
This is not the term used.
“The silver spoon”
The review’s title mentions a silver spoon, but the disease is named differently.
“Fortune sickness”
This is not the term used.
“Affluenza”
Some wealthy people limit their children’s legacies because of it.
questions.rationale: As Richard Watts says, “More money, more problems.” A life of contentment is better than aspiring to more and more wealth.

questions.q: What does the article identify as the root of all human problems?
options: People want to build their paradise in the world before death
Under the system of nature, this world is not made for that.
People do not work hard enough
The article’s point is about expectation, not effort.
People live too long
This is not suggested.
People have too little knowledge of science
This is not the cause given.
questions.rationale: Hardship is part of the creation plan: this world is a place of trial, and Paradise is in store in the world after death for those who live here with contentment.

questions.q: Which short chapter of the Quran does this article draw its lesson from?
options: Al Fatihah (The Opening)
This is not the chapter discussed.
Al Asr (Time)
This is not the chapter discussed.
Al Tin (The Fig)
‘We have indeed created man in the best of moulds…’ (95:4-5)
Al Ikhlas (Oneness)
This is not the chapter discussed.
questions.rationale: The human personality has plus points and minus points. Used to the best advantage it makes a super achiever; used rashly it reduces a person to zero.
